```{r}

#Load Required Package


library(palmerpenguins)
# install.packages("dplyr")
library(dplyr)

#Load the Penguins Data Set
data(penguins)


#View the first few rows
head(penguins)

#setup
#number of rows
nrow(penguins)

#number of columns
ncol(penguins)

#data types
str(penguins)

#Question 1.1:
# Extract bill_length_mm as a vector
bill_lengths <- c(pull(penguins, bill_len))

# Calculate: mean, median, sd, min, max (handle NAs!)
mean(bill_lengths, na.rm = TRUE)
median(bill_lengths, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(bill_lengths, na.rm = TRUE)
min(bill_lengths, na.rm = TRUE)
max(bill_lengths, na.rm = TRUE)

#Question 1.2
# Create logical vector: TRUE when bill length > 45mm
long_bills <- bill_lengths > 45

# How many penguins have long bills?
sum(long_bills == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)

#Question 2.1
# Extract bill lengths for Dream island penguins only
dream_bl <- pull(filter(penguins, island == "Dream"), bill_len)

# Calculate the mean for this subset
mean(dream_bl, na.rm = TRUE)

#Question 2.2
# How many Adelie penguins are in the dataset?
adel_peng <- pull(filter(penguins, species == "Adelie"))
sum(adel_peng)

#Question 2.3
# Find: body mass, species, and island of the heaviest penguin
heaviest_peng <- max(penguins$body_mass, na.rm = TRUE)
g<- penguins[penguins$body_mass == heaviest_peng, c("body_mass", "species", "island") ]

#Question 3.1
# Remove rows with missing values
penguins_complete <- penguins[complete.cases(penguins), ]

#Create matrix with: bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, 
#flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g
bill_length_mm <- c(pull(penguins_complete, bill_len))
bill_depth_mm <- c(pull(penguins_complete, bill_dep))
flipper_length_mm <- c(pull(penguins_complete, flipper_len))
body_mass_g <- c(pull(penguins_complete, body_mass))

# Create matrix with: bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, 
# flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g
penguin_measurements1 <- cbind(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g)

#Question 3.2
# Use apply() to calculate mean of each column
apply(penguin_measurements1, 2, mean)

# Use apply() to find which row has the maximum for each column
apply(penguin_measurements1, 2, max)

#Question 4.1
#Function that: removes NAs, returns (x - mean) / sd
standardize <- function(x) { }
```
